title: A machine learning assay to predict disease recurrence in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.
authors: Boscolo Bielo, L; Trapani, D; Razavi, P; Chandarlapaty, S; Zhan, Y; Curigliano, G
one_liner_zh: 该研究开发基于14基因表达特征的机器学习模型预测乳腺癌复发风险，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor 2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer associates with a sustained risk of relapse over time. Current multigene assays offer limited validity to identify clinically low-risk tumors at high risk of recurrence, which is particularly relevant in the context of novel adjuvant therapies. In this study, we developed and validated ER-Predict, a machine learning assay leveraging a 14-gene expression signature to classify early stage HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer according to the risk of relapse. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ER-Predict was developed on a cohort of 1413 HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer cases. External validation was carried out across eight publicly available cohorts (n = 1118). Comparative benchmarking was conducted against reproduced prognostic signatures, and particularly, EndoPredict and Oncotype DX. Functional annotation and drug response analysis were carried out using gene expression and pharmacogenomic data from publicly available breast cancer cell lines. RESULTS: ER-Predict identified high-risk patients with significantly reduced distant metastasis-free survival in the external validation cohort (hazard ratio 2.03, 95% confidence interval 1.57-2.63, P < 0.0001). The assay demonstrated independent prognostic value beyond traditional clinicopathological factors, including tumor grade, tumor size, and nodal status, and consistently outperformed recomputed multigene panels. ER-Predict showed specificity toward luminal-like transcriptomic programs, revealing activation of key cell-cycle regulators governing endocrine resistance among high-risk tumors that had retained expression of retinoblastoma-1, suggesting potential actionability by means of cell-cycle inhibitors. CONCLUSIONS: ER-Predict represents a robust assay with potential utility in early stage HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer. Its consistent ability to identify high-risk patients supports further investigation as a decision-support tool to guide treatment intensification in clinically low-risk HR-positive/HER2-negative disease.
abstract_zh: 背景：激素受体（HR）阳性、人表皮生长因子受体2（HER2）阴性乳腺癌与随时间推移的持续复发风险相关。当前的多基因检测在识别临床低风险但复发风险高的肿瘤方面有效性有限，这在新型辅助治疗背景下尤为重要。在本研究中，我们开发并验证了ER-Predict，一种利用14基因表达特征的机器学习检测方法，用于根据复发风险对早期HR阳性/HER2阴性乳腺癌进行分类。材料与方法：ER-Predict在1413例HR阳性/HER2阴性早期乳腺癌病例队列中开发。外部验证在八个公开可用队列（n = 1118）中进行。与复现的预后特征进行了比较基准测试，特别是EndoPredict和Oncotype DX。使用公开可用的乳腺癌细胞系的基因表达和药物基因组学数据进行了功能注释和药物反应分析。结果：ER-Predict在外部验证队列中识别出远处无转移生存期显著缩短的高风险患者（风险比2.03，95%置信区间1.57-2.63，P < 0.0001）。该检测方法显示出超越传统临床病理因素（包括肿瘤分级、肿瘤大小和淋巴结状态）的独立预后价值，并持续优于重新计算的多基因面板。ER-Predict对腔面样转录组程序表现出特异性，揭示在高风险肿瘤中，尽管保留了视网膜母细胞瘤蛋白1的表达，但调控内分泌耐药的关键细胞周期调节因子被激活，提示通过细胞周期抑制剂可能具有可操作性。结论：ER-Predict代表了一种稳健的检测方法，在早期HR阳性/HER2阴性乳腺癌中具有潜在应用价值。其持续识别高风险患者的能力支持其作为决策支持工具的进一步研究，以指导临床低风险HR阳性/HER2阴性疾病的治疗强化。
